wiki_catalogs.name: Project Overview
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for the CareBridge project overview section focused on the autonomous care coordination system. Explain its purpose as a multi-agent AI system that automates elderly care coordination through medication management, appointment scheduling, delivery logistics, and family communication. Document the problem statement addressing caregiver burden and medication adherence challenges. Describe the target users including caregivers, care recipients, and family members. Include the system's value proposition of owning the end-to-end coordination workflow. Provide both conceptual overviews for beginners understanding care coordination challenges and technical details for developers implementing similar systems. Use terminology consistent with the codebase including terms like 'care recipient', 'escalation logic', and 'audit trail'. Include practical examples demonstrating common care scenarios like medication refill monitoring and appointment coordination.

Include the Strands Agents SDK integration with graceful degradation when unavailable. Provide concrete examples of event processing flows, escalation scenarios, and error handling patterns. wiki_overview.content:
# CareBridge: AI-Powered Care Coordination System ## Project Introduction CareBridge is an AI-powered care coordination system designed to help caregivers manage the complex logistics of elderly care. The system orchestrates medication refills, appointment scheduling, delivery coordination, and family communication through a sophisticated multi-agent architecture powered by the Strands Agents SDK. ### Purpose Statement CareBridge automates the coordination tasks that typically fall on adult children caring for aging parents, reducing cognitive load and ensuring critical care events are never missed. ### Core Goals and Objectives - **Automated Medication Management**: Monitor refill levels and automatically order prescriptions when needed - **Appointment Coordination**: Track upcoming appointments and send preparation reminders - **Delivery Logistics**: Coordinate pharmacy deliveries and grocery orders with retry logic - **Family Communication**: Keep family members informed through SMS and email alerts - **Audit Trail**: Maintain immutable records of all actions for compliance and transparency ### Target Audience - Adult children caring for aging parents - Professional caregivers managing multiple clients - Healthcare coordination teams ## Technical Architecture The system follows a sophisticated multi-agent architecture where specialized agents handle specific domains while a supervisor agent orchestrates the overall workflow. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph "User Layer" CG[Caregiver Dashboard] FM[Family Members
SMS/Email] CR[Care Recipient] end subgraph "CareBridge Core" SUP[Supervisor Agent] subgraph "Specialized Agents" MED[Medication Agent] APT[Appointment Agent] LOG[Logistics Agent] COM[Communication Agent] end AUD[(Immutable Audit Trail)] ESC[Escalation Logic] end subgraph "External Services" PHAR[Pharmacy API] CAL[Calendar API] MSG[Messaging Service] DEL[Delivery Service] end CG --> SUP FM -.-> MSG CR -.-> COM SUP --> MED SUP --> APT SUP --> LOG SUP --> COM MED --> PHAR APT --> CAL LOG --> DEL COM --> MSG SUP --> AUD SUP --> ESC ``` ### Component Breakdown **Supervisor Agent**: Central orchestrator that routes events to specialized agents and manages escalation decisions **Medication Agent**: Handles prescription refills, adherence monitoring, and pharmacy coordination **Appointment Agent**: Manages calendar scheduling, appointment reminders, and provider coordination **Logistics Agent**: Coordinates deliveries, grocery orders, and transportation services **Communication Agent**: Sends alerts, notifications, and status updates to family members ### Design Patterns - **Agent-as-Tools Pattern**: Each specialized agent operates as a callable tool within the supervisor's context - **Event-Driven Architecture**: Care events flow through the system with deterministic routing - **Immutable Audit Trail**: Every action is logged before execution using SQLite with triggers preventing modifications - **Retry with Exponential Backoff**: External API calls use standardized retry logic (3 attempts, 1s/2s/4s delays) - **Deterministic Escalation**: Safety-critical decisions use hardcoded rules rather than LLM judgment ### System Relationships The system maintains strict separation of concerns where specialized agents never call each other directly—all coordination flows through the supervisor agent. This ensures consistent audit logging and prevents circular dependencies. ## Key Implementation ### Main Entry Points - **`main.py`**: Application bootstrap that initializes the audit database, loads fixtures, and runs the demo scenario - **`src/agents/supervisor_agent.py`**: Core orchestration logic with event routing and escalation management ### Core Modules - **`src/models/schemas.py`**: Pydantic v2 data models defining the contract between all components - **`src/models/audit_log.py`**: Immutable SQLite audit trail with triggers preventing UPDATE/DELETE operations - **`src/models/escalation_logic.py`**: Deterministic classification engine for safety-critical decisions ### Configuration Approach - **`requirements.txt`**: Python dependencies including Strands Agents SDK, Pydantic, and testing frameworks - **`pyproject.toml`**: Pytest configuration for async test support - **`fixtures/`**: JSON fixture files providing mock data for medications, appointments, family members, and delivery history ### External Dependencies - **Strands Agents SDK**: Multi-agent orchestration framework - **Pydantic v2**: Data validation and serialization - **SQLite**: Local database for audit trail during development - **Boto3**: AWS integration for production deployment ### Integration Points - **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**: In-process SDK servers for pharmacy, messaging, and delivery services - **Google Calendar API**: External calendar integration via SSE transport - **Twilio/SendGrid**: Messaging services for SMS and email notifications ### Component Relationship Diagrams ```mermaid classDiagram class SupervisorAgent { +process_event(event) ResolutionResult +query_status(recipient_id, question) str +approve_pending_action(action_id, approved) None -_route_to_agent(event) tuple -_evaluate_escalation(event, result) tuple } class SpecializedAgents { <> +handle_medication_event() +handle_appointment_event() +handle_logistics_event() +handle_communication_event() } class AuditTrail { +write_audit_event() +get_audit_events() +init_audit_db() } class EscalationLogic { +classify_action() AUTONOMOUS_ACTIONS REQUIRES_ALERT REQUIRES_APPROVAL } SupervisorAgent --> SpecializedAgents SupervisorAgent --> AuditTrail SupervisorAgent --> EscalationLogic ``` ## Key Features ### Functionality Overview **Medication Management**: Automatically monitors prescription refill levels and places orders when supplies run low, with intelligent adherence tracking to detect missed doses or irregular patterns. **Appointment Coordination**: Tracks upcoming medical appointments, sends preparation checklists, and coordinates transportation needs for elderly care recipients. **Delivery Logistics**: Manages pharmacy deliveries and grocery orders with robust retry logic and failure escalation to ensure essential items reach their destination. **Family Communication**: Keeps family members informed through automated SMS and email alerts about care activities, medication changes, and appointment updates. ### Implementation Highlights - **Immutable Audit Trail**: Every action is recorded in SQLite with database triggers preventing any modification or deletion, ensuring complete accountability - **Deterministic Escalation**: Safety-critical decisions use hardcoded business rules rather than LLM judgment, eliminating hallucination risks - **Robust Retry Logic**: All external API calls implement exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) with automatic escalation after three failures - **Graceful Degradation**: System falls back to deterministic routing when Strands SDK or Bedrock credentials are unavailable ### Feature Architecture ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> EventReceived EventReceived --> RouteToAgent: Classify event type RouteToAgent --> ProcessAgent: Execute specialized logic ProcessAgent --> CheckEscalation: Evaluate outcome CheckEscalation --> Success: No escalation needed CheckEscalation --> AlertRequired: Alert level escalation CheckEscalation --> ApprovalRequired: Human approval needed AlertRequired --> NotifyFamily: Send SMS/email ApprovalRequired --> QueueForApproval: Wait for human decision NotifyFamily --> Success: Notification sent QueueForApproval --> Success: Action approved QueueForApproval --> Rejected: Action rejected Success --> [*] Rejected --> [*] ``` The system processes care events through a structured workflow that ensures every action is properly classified, audited, and executed with appropriate safeguards. The deterministic escalation logic provides predictable behavior for safety-critical scenarios while maintaining flexibility for routine operations.
